product_brief: PKI and digital signature server providing CA, OCSP, signing, verification and timestamping services, with ML-DSA and ML-KEM PQC support.
pqc_support: Yes — ML-DSA-44/65/87 and ML-KEM-512/768/1024 supported across CA, CRL, OCSP, CMS signing and timestamp services since ADSS Server 8.3.5
pqc_capability_description: ADSS Server 8.3.5 (July 2024) introduced production-grade PQC across signing and PKI services; 8.4 focused on standards conformance for ML-DSA (RFC 9881 for certificates/CRLs, RFC 9882 for CMS). ML-DSA used for X.509 certificates, CRLs, OCSP, CMS and timestamp tokens. ML-KEM supported in SPKI structures for quantum-safe certificates and hybrid deployments.
architecture_type: Centralized server (on-prem/self-hosted); version 8.4.0 adds cloud-native containerised deployment (Docker) without HSM integration yet
primary_platforms: Java-based server (JDK 17, Apache Tomcat); Docker/container orchestration; Oracle and Microsoft SQL Server databases
target_industries: Enterprises, trust service providers, government organisations
regulatory_status: Common Criteria certified at EAL4+ assurance level (Key Management Systems category)
pqc_roadmap_details: ML-KEM/ML-DSA already supported; FALCON noted as slated for upcoming standardisation; HSM-backed PQC deployments to be covered in a later article in the series; HSM integration for containerised deployments planned for a future release.
signature_schemes: ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65, ML-DSA-87 (current); RSA and ECDSA classical comparisons mentioned; FALCON noted as upcoming NIST standard
testing_&_validation_methods: Downloadable ML-DSA artefacts (certificates, CRL, CMS, OCSP, timestamp token) for independent validation; interoperability testing with OpenSSL 3.6.1 and Bouncy Castle 1.83 planned in next article
deployment_&_migration_complexity: PQC fits existing PKIX/CMS/OCSP/TSP structures without redesigning trust model; challenge is operational/performance due to larger keys and signatures; hybrid classical/PQC deployment supported.

evidence.PQC Support: With ADSS Server 8.3.5 (released July 2024) , Ascertia introduced production-grade PQC support across signing and PKI services.
evidence.PQC Capability Description: ADSS Server aligns with the NIST PQC standardisation effort and supports finalised ML-DSA and ML-KEM parameter sets.
evidence.Latest Version: Ascertia ADSS CA Server 8.4.0 introduces a next-generation Certificate Authority architecture
evidence.FIPS Validated: Ascertia ADSS Server has completed Common Criteria certification at the EAL4+ Assurance Level.
evidence.Signature Schemes: With another algorithm, FALCON, also slated for upcoming standardisation.
evidence.PQC Roadmap Details: Support for HSM integration in containerised environments is planned for a future release.

product_brief: Core component of the open source ILM platform providing certificate lifecycle management and cryptographic key inventory, with ACME, SCEP and CMP protocol support.
pqc_support: Yes — ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, ML-KEM and FALCON (FN-DSA) supported in Core
pqc_capability_description: The document states that Core supports the PQC algorithms ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, ML-KEM and FALCON (FN-DSA). No maturity level, versions or implementation details are given.
key_management_model: Keys and certificates are abstracted through Profiles (RA Profile, Token Profile, Compliance Profile); a key inventory is managed via the Token Profile, which configures the cryptographic service and key management. Key hierarchy, root key protection, escrow and rotation policies are not stated.
architecture_type: Centralized Core service with Connectors for specific technologies; delivered as a Docker container; depends on an Auth service, OPA, a database, a scheduler service and a message broker (RabbitMQ or Azure Service Bus)
primary_platforms: Docker container (image hub.omnitrustregistry.com/ilm/core:tagname); Java-based (JAVA_OPTS); Azure Service Bus integration supported
cryptographic_discovery_&_inventory: Certificate inventory contains all certificates that were discovered or imported; key inventory contains all keys available for use, managed via the Token Profile. CBOM and algorithm enumeration are not stated.
supply_chain_&_vendor_risk: Open source project (ILM); depends on separate auth service and auth-opa-policies repositories, OPA, and a message broker.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Core fails to run if the Auth service or OPA is missing; requires database, scheduler service, message broker and trusted certificate store configuration via environment variables; OPA may run as a sidecar on the same host. Migration phases and rollback are not stated.
